articleTitle: Digital Integrated Circuits II
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: This session focuses on emerging high speed GaAs digital technologies and state-of-the-art performance from advanced development GaAs technology.

articleTitle: Optoelectronic Circuits
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: This session will address the future needs for high speed, large capacity data communication links which utilize multi-Gbs optical links. The papers describe integrated Optoelectronic transmitters and receivers. The emphasis is on the monolithic integration of the optical transmitter and receiver devices with high speed digital circuits.

articleTitle: Digital Integrated Circuits (I)
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: GaAs ICs are making rapid advances in signal processing speed as well as in scale of integration. This session starts with an overview of important applications of GaAs ICs in high speed data processing. Next, circuits are described which demonstrate A/D and D/A conversion at gigabit rates.

articleTitle: Power Amplifiers and Special Purpose Circuits
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Significant advances have been made in the operating frequency and bandwidth for monolithic GaAs power amplifiers and for special purpose MMICs. A multi-octave 2 W power amplifier and medium power amplifiers operating up to 20 GHz are reported.

articleTitle: Small Signal Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Significant progress has been made in developing low noise GaAs monolithic microwave integrated circuits (MMICs) for both commercial and military applications. The technology is now capable of addressing wide bandwidth requirements from 0.1 to beyond 20 GHz. A relatively new device structure, the two-dimensional electron gas FET (TEGFET) promises to further extend the performance capability of MMICs.

articleTitle: Processing
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Important new developments in GaAs processing technology will be presented in this session. It will begin with the characterization of a promising new metal for self-aligned gate FETs, W-Al. Next, another self-aligned process utilizing an "SiO<inf>2</inf> gate" will be described. The next two papers discuss side-gating and how the conduction characteristics of GaAs surfaces are affected by various treatments and dielectric coatings. A paper on a model for analyzing the yield on GaAs ICs will be presented, and finally, the effects of increasing the doping in FET channels will be examined.

articleTitle: Materials
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: High quality semi-insulating GaAs is essential for the fabrication of GaAs integrated circuits. In this session the status of GaAs materials technology is reviewed, the electrical uniformities of Si implanted LEC and HB grown semi-insulating material are compared, and a method is presented for improving the uniformity of LEC material. Finally, the application of MBE to the investigation of the effects of channel doping on FET properties is discussed.

articleTitle: Charge Coupled Devices
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: This session has two papers on CCDs. The first paper addresses their application to transversal filters, and multiplexing and demultiplexing operations. The second paper presents a new approach for establishing efficient charge transfer.

articleTitle: Radiation Effects
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: This session will begin with an invited overview of how GaAs integrated circuits are affected by radiation. The physical mechanisms involved in both long term radiation and single event upsets will be examined, and the existing data base will be reviewed. A second paper will present measurements of the position dependence of the response of GaAs devices to transient ionized radiation.

articleTitle: The GaAs IC Industry Structure - Present and Future
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Companies in Europe, Japan, and the United States have now achieved satisfactory and consistent yields on limited production runs of GaAs ICs. Several GaAs ICs have been successfully designed and tested with LSI levels of complexity. Numerous applications have been defined requiring the high speed performance characteristics of the GaAs technology. However, the emergence of a merchant market for GaAs ICs is proceeding in a painfully slow manner.

articleTitle: Side-Gating in GaAs Integrated Circuits: Surface and Bulk Related Phenomena
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: We haue studied side-gating for GaAs ICs fabricated by direct ion implantation in a SI substrate. Different types of side-gate electrodes (n,p and AuGe: Ni on SI GaAs) have been used together with different geometrical configurations. The electrode separations used ranged from 10 $$um to 200 $$um. The most spectacular effect we have observed is the that the Side-Gating (SG) threshold is very strongly affected by different types of surface treatments of the unprotected GaAs surface. A class of chemical surface treatments reduce this effect by multiplying its negative threshold potential by factors up to 3. Other treatments significantly increase the leakage currents between mesa-insulated electrodes while simultaneously aggravating SG. We also observe that SG from a p-type electrode only occurs for positive electrode potentials. A detailed analysis of our experimental results has led us to a physical model for SG effects. The n-type SG electrode injects electrons into the SI substrate which are then trapped by compensating deep levels, thus leading to a negative space charge accumulation layer at the MESFET channel-substrate interface. The physics for the formation of this layer resembles that occurring in Gunn diodes. The presence of a random heterogeneous surface leakage conduction may lead to local increases in the microscopic fields and can significantly aggravate side-gating.

articleTitle: X-Band Receive Module using Monolithic GaAs MMIC's
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: An X-band solid state receive module for use in active phased array antenna systems is described. The module, which includes microwave integrated circuits (MMIC's) monolithically grown on gallium arsenide, consists of a limiter, low noise amplifier, and three-bit phase shifter. The assembly is packaged within the element spacing constraints of an SHF SATCOM conformai array. 128 modules utilizing over 500 monolithic ICs were fabricated and assembled into an ADM receive-only phased array, successfully demonstrating active conformai array technology using monolithic gallium arsenide devices on a large scale. 30 one-inch wafers of GaAs were processed to produce the 128 three-bit phase shifters resulting in a remarkable 16% yield for the complete "production" run. This represents a significant step toward large-scale development and implementation of GaAs ICs in operational systems.

articleTitle: Present and Projected Status of GaAs Materials Technology
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The quality of GaAs substrates for integrated circuits (IC) is critically important since device yield is effected by defects and electrical nonuniformity. The crystal growth technique effects the type and quality of the substrate. Liquid encapsulated Czochralski (LEC) substrates can be prepared semi-insulating (SI) without chromium additions (1) but most horizontal Bridgman crystals (HB) require chromium. Chromium can play an important role in the processing steps and the final electrical prooerties of an integrated circuit (2). In snite of chromium, recent results indicate that dislocation density could be thè decisive factor in the choice of substrates. Looking further ahead other important factors are: 1. Number of slices per crystal, 2. Substrate size, 3. Cost, and 4. Availability. This presentation is an attempt to define the present situation and try to project the future status of GaAs substrate technology.

articleTitle: Yield Analysis Methods for GaAs ICs
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Yield of a GaAs IC is determined by subsubstrate defects, device parameter variations, and process-induced defects. This paper will describe theoretical upper and lower bound parameter yield models for a DCFL E-JFET inverter with resistive load. A Monte-Carlo analysis with SPICE 2 is also performed to predict yield (1). A GaAs process evaluation chip will be discussed. Data from this chip will be compared to the parameter limited yield estimates.

articleTitle: Ultra High Speed Digital Integrated Circuits using GaAs/GaAlAs High Electron Mobility Transistors
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Ultra high speed integrated circuits using planar processed high electron mobility transistors have been fabricated. The lowest propagation delay measured from 25-stage ring oscillators at room temperature is 12.2 ps. Divide-by-four circuits with two T-connected D-flip flops are capable of operating at 3.48 GHz for 0.47 mW per gate at room temperature. The speed-power products achieved are the lowest ever reported.

articleTitle: Improved Uniformity of LEC Undoped Gallium Arsenide Produced by High Temperature Annealing
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The annealing of whole ingots of undoped LEC gallium arsenide reduces radial variations on resistivity and mobility to less than ± 10% and reduces seed-to-tail variations. In general the mean value of mobilities is increased. Measurements of the deep level (EL2) concentration by infra-red imaging shows a reduction of both the basic 'W' variation and the superimposed fine structure is not affected. Dislocation densities and distribution appear to be unaffected by the annealing process.

articleTitle: Emitter-Coupled Logic Circuits Implemented with Heterojunction Bipolar Transistors
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: This paper describes the first experimental demonstration of ECL circuits using (Ga,Al)As/GaAs heterojunction bipolar transistors. Ringoscillators were fabricated which exhibited propagation delay times as low as 185 ps, with devices fabricated on the basis of 2 μm design rules. Potential advantages of GaAs ECL circuits, their fabrication technology and their expected future performance are also discussed.

articleTitle: A High Yield GaAs Gate Array Technology and Applications
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: An LSI GaAs gate array consisting of 1224 DCFL gates and 66 I/O buffers has been demonstrated using E/D MESFET technology. The chip dimensions are 4.6 × 43 mm<sup>2</sup> and it contains 6978 FET's. The key process features are: 1) selective ion-implantation, 2) recessed 1 μιη gates to reduce source-gate parasitic resistance, 3) custom first level interconnect layer and 4) custom airbridge interconnections for second layer metal. The threshold voltages for the Ε-mode and the D-mode FET's are V<inf>T</inf> = 0.2 V and V<inf>P</inf> = -0.5 V respectively. The best g<inf>m</inf> for the Ε-mode FET was measured to be 200 mS/mm. The DCFL gate has a typical propagation delay of 100 ps at 250 μW/gate and the best propagation delay achieved was 52 ps at 550 μW/gate. A pseudo-random sequence generator (140 gates) and an 8-bit serial multiplier (410 gates) have shown yields of 65% and 35% respectively.

articleTitle: Gigabit Optoelectronic Transmitters
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: An integrated optoelectronic transmitter chip which combines small-scale (36 SDFL NOR gates) GaAs electronics with a semiconductor laser has been fabricated and tested. The transmitter contains a 4:1 multiplexer, a power driver, and a transverse junction stripe laser. The MESFETs in the multiplexer and driver are fabricated using selective ion implantation into a semi-insulating substrate and have 1 micron-gate lengths. The fully monolithically integrated laser/multiplexer has thus far been operated at 160 MHz clock rates. This is the first time that a laser has been successfully integrated with both a GaAs digital circuit and the FETs which drive the laser.

articleTitle: 0.25 mW, 1.9 GHz, GaAs Τ Flip-Flops
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: GaAs Τ flip-flops with a power consumption as low as 0.25 mW at a maximum operating frequency of 1.9 GHz have been fabricated using a dynamic DCFL approach. These TFF's have the lowest power consumption ever reported at this frequency. Direct comparison with a static approach has been made using the same N-off process. A reduction in power consumption of about a factor 40 has been observed between both approaches. The minimum frequency of operation is 50 MHz. It is quasi-constant up to 350°K whereas the maximum frequency of operation has a negative temperature coefficient of about - 2 MHz/°C between 100°K and 350°K.

articleTitle: An ECL Compatible 4 BIT GaAs Universal Shift Register, Binary Counter Chip Set for Gigahertz System Operation
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Two MSI GaAs ICs will be described which have been designed, fabricated and extensively tested. The devices are a 4 bit universal shift register (Fig. 1) and a synchronous divide by 2, 4, and 8 binary counter (Ref.1). Their unique features include the following: (1) on chip ECL and GaAs I/O buffering, (2) a fully decoded and cascadable shift register, and, (3) both devices exhibiting gigahertz operation on wafer and in a commercial 32 pin package (Ref. 2). Both parts are slated for commercial introduction in 1983 and will represent the first GaAs IC products of their kind available.

articleTitle: A GHz GaAs Digital to Analog Converter
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A monolithic 4-bit digital to analog converter (DAC) with 100 ps rise and fall times has been built using depletion-mode GaAs MESFETs. The output settles to within 1% of full scale (800 mV into 25 ohms) in 1 ns at rates up to 1 gigasample per second (GS/s), and to within 0.75% in 1.3 ns at rates up to 660 MS/s. Good matching and scaling of the on-chip binary-weighted current sources was achieved. Eleven out of 196 DACs (5%) measured at DC showed a maximum error of 0.2% of full scale which is equivalent to an accuracy of 8 bits ±1/2 of a least significant bit (LSB). Forty-eight percent of the DACs worked; most of them had an accuracy in the 6 to 8 bit range.

articleTitle: A Radiation-Hard Low-Power GaAs Static RAM using E-JFET DCFL
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A fully decoded GaAs 256 by' 1 static RAM has been designed and fabricated with all 256 cells functional. The design utilizes DCFL gates with enhancement mode JFETs and resistive loads. N type resistors are used in the peripheral gating circuitry and high value Ρ type resistors in the memory cells. The circuit contains 1794 FETs with 1 µm gate lengths. The best access time measures 6.5 nsec, with 10 nsec typical. Cycle time is typically 20 nsec. Operating power of the circuit is quite low at 30 mW, with a standby power of 1.5 mW.

articleTitle: Transversal Filter Application of A High Speed Gallium Arsenide CCD
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Substantial progress toward the incorporation of a 1 GHz continuous clock rate GaAs CCD in a monolithic transversal filter design has been achieved. This paper will discuss performance results for the GaAs CCD at frequencies from 1 MHz to 1000 MHz. This device performs with a CTE of at least 0.999 per transfer at 1 GHz continuous clocking, measured by the magnitude response of the modulation transfer function. A half-banding analog filter is described in detail. The CCDs in the filter are arranged in a pipe-organ structure and provide three important signal processing functions in the charge domain: weighted sampling, programmable delay, and accurate summing. The current design specifications provide for a clock rate from below 50 MHz to in excess of 900 MHz, corresponding to an input bandwidth of 0 to 450 MHz. The filter will select the upper or lower half band of the input. This design allows for convenient cascading of chips to provide narrower passbands and higher out-of-band attenuation. Since these are complex band-pass filters, there is an in-phase branch and a quadrature branch in the complete filter. The current developments have stemmed from work previously reported (1) and from the obvious need to incorporate GaAs CCDs with suitable high speed support circuits. Therefore, the device has been mono!ithically integrated with MESFET IC technology to enable its use in circuit applications where the 1 GHz GaAs CCD has performance advantages. This VHF/UHF filter is a good example of such applications.

articleTitle: A 256×4 BIT GaAs Static RAM
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A 256×4 bit GaAs Static RAM was fabricated by Pt-buried gate FET process technology. Chip size was 2.9mm × 4.0mm. A six transistor depletion load cell was employed as a unit memory cell. Cell size was 65 µm × 67 µm. All of the peripheral circuits were E/D DCFLs with 1.2 µm gate, except for sense amplifiers. To compare the sensing performances, four different types of sense amplifiers were implemented for four output bits in a single memory chip. The minimum X address access time, which was measured on a wafer with a probe card modified and calibrated for 50-ohm testing circuit, was 4.0ns. Power dissipation was 160-190 mW at the power supply voltage of 2.0 V.

articleTitle: 6-19 GHz GaAs FET Transmit-Receive Switch
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The distributed FET switch concept is applied to the development of a wideband single-pole double-throw monolithic switch. The switch operates in the 6-19 GHz frequency band with less than 2 dB insertion loss and better than 30 dB isolation across the full band. Switching times as short as 0.2 nsec have been measured.

articleTitle: A Wide Band Medium Power Monolithic Microwave Amplifier
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A monolithic GaAs power amplifier stage has been designed for operation in the Ku (12 to 18 GHz) band. The planar monolithic circuit employs a 1400 μ FET (Lg $$ 0.7 µm). The design goal for output power was 0.5 W. Eight gate feeds were used on the FET, both to minimize gate resistance losses and to assure equal phase of the input signal along the gate. Symmetry of the input and output matching networks further maintain constant phase at equivalent points on different signal paths. Preliminary test results provided gains of greater than 7 dB from 14 to 18 GHz, and a 0.3 W power output. Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit (MMIC) technology makes possible the implementation of entire amplifier functions as a single chip. Such single chip amplifiers include the FET and matching circuits. The matching circuits are realized with passive elements, including transmission lines. Broadband operation is possible. Of interest for many applications is a substantial output power. This paper describes an amplifier design for the 12 to 18 GHz frequency range that is matched to maximize output power, and implemented as a MMIC.

articleTitle: Radiation Effects in GaAs Integrated Circuits: A Comparison with Silicon
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: This paper reviews the hardness capability of contemporary GaAs devices and logic circuits in terms of the four major nuclear and space radiation threat categories—neutron effects, total dose effects, dose rate effects, and single particle phenomena. The basic interaction mechanisms for each threat area are briefly described,, with emphasis given to potential problem areas and to fundamental differences between gallium arsenide and silicon. Existing and projected hardness levels characteristic of GaAs devices are compared with corresponding levels for silicon LSI technologies.

articleTitle: A Three-Stage Power Amplifier for A 20 GHz Monolithic Transmit Module
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Design, fabrication, and test results of a three-stage GaAs monolithic power amplifier covering the 17.7 to 20.2 GHz band are described in this paper. Intermediate results for single and two-stage amplifiers are also presented. The 1.5 × 3.1 millimeter three-stage amplifier chip has 15 dB gain from 16.5 to 20.2 GHz. Measured saturated output power is between +20 and +21 dBm with improvement expected from minor circuit and device changes.

articleTitle: 12 GHz-BAND GaAs Dual-Gate Mesfet Monolithic Mixers
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: 12 GHz-band GaAs dual-gate MESFET monolithic mixers have been developed for use in direct broadcasting satellite receivers. In order to reduce chip size, a buffer amplifier has been connected directly after a mixer IF port, instead of employing an IF matching circuit. The mixer and the buffer were fabricated on separate chips, so that individual measurements could be achieved. Chip size is 0.96 × 1.26 mm for the mixer and 0.96 × 0.60 mm for the buffer. A dual-gate FET for the mixer, as well as a single-gate FET for the buffer, has a closely-spaced electrode structure. Gate length and width are 1 phn and 320 µm, respectively. The mixer with the buffer provides 2.9 ± 0.4 dB conversion gain with 12.3± 0.3 dB SSB noise figure in the 11.7 to 12.2 GHz RF band. LO frequency is 10.8 GHz. A low-noise converter was constructed by connecting a monolithic pre-amplifier, an image rejection filter and a monolithic IF amplifier to the mixer. The converter provides 46.8 ±1.5 dB conversion gain with 2.81 0.2 dB SSB noise figure in the same frequency band.

articleTitle: Accurate Coupling Predictions and Assessments in MMIC Networks
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A major design requirement for GaAs MMIC networks is a knowledge of the coupling properties between transmission lines and within active switches. This is believed to be the first report on coupling effects between conductors spaced by more than a substrate thickness (h). Measurements and predictions are given on over 20 circuits for (i) coupled line pairs, with and without intervening shielding lines, (ii) transmission line crossover networks, and (iii) switching amplifier applications.

articleTitle: Self-Aligned Pt-Buried Gate FET Process with Surface Planarization Technique for GaAs LSI
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A self-aligned Pt-buried gate FET process has been developed. It is featured by the formation of "SiO<inf>2</inf> gate" for N<sup>+</sup> ion implantation mask and the surface planarization-etching technique to convert the "SiO<inf>2</inf> gate" into a "Pt gate". A normally-off FET with a 1.1µm gate was successfully fab­ricated. Observed average transconductance was 200 mS/mm.

articleTitle: 20 GHz Two Stage Low Noise Monolithic Amplifier
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A 20 GHz two stage monolithic GaAs amplifier was designed, fabricated and evaluated. The two stage amplifier used 350 µm FETs with a π-gate feed. The matching networks were optimized using COMPACT to achieve the desired gain and noise figure. A Fukui model was used for the FET. A noise figure of 5 dB with an associated gain of 9 dB at 20 GHz has been measured.

articleTitle: Properties of Surface Passivation Dielectrics for GaAs Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Electrical properties of surface passivation films for GaAs ICs were studied by measuring the surface I-V characteristics on semi-insulating wafers and the surface state parameters. Silicon dioxide and silicon nitride films were formed by plasma CVD processes. Characteristic activation energies of 0.3-0.5 eV were observed in both linear and superlinear regions of I-V curves and in electron emission from surface states, which suggests surface state conduction. It is shown that surface passivation becomes increasingly important in GaAs VLSIs.

articleTitle: HEMT LSI Technology for High Speed Computers
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: High Electron Mobility Transistor (HEMT) LSI technology based on selectively doped GaAs/AlGaAs heterojunction structure for high speed computer application is described. Diagnostic patterns including HEMT test device groups are fabricated to encompass a number of interrelated material and device processing parameters. By evaluating the gate length dependence of threshold voltage and K-factor of short channel HEMTs and their uniformity over the wafer, HEMT is confirmed to be suitable for high performance LSI devices. Master-slave flip-flop divide-by-two circuits are implemented, operating at clock frequencies as high as 8.9 GHz with power dissipation of 2.8 mW/gate at 77K. This corresponds to a logic delay of 22 ps/gate, roughly three times faster than that of GaAs MESFET technology. The top down design of the HEMT based computer is performed. System performance is projected to a system clock cycle time of 2 ns to achieve computer performance of over 120 MIPS.

articleTitle: Electrical Uniformity of LEC- and Hb-Grown, Semi-Insulating GaAs Crystals Implanted with Si
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Electrical homogeneities of LEC- and HB-grown, semi-insulating crystals were characterized by Hall measurement and FET threshold voltage, after Si ion implantation followed by annealing, and the differences between them are compared. For LEC crystals, electrical properties and threshold voltage (Vth) reproducibilities exhibited to be better than those for HB crystals. But Vth deviation in small area was smaller for HB crystals than that for LEC crystals.

articleTitle: Improved Performance of Micron and Submicron GATE GaAs Mesfets Due to High Electron Concentrations (n = 1018 cm-3) in the Channel
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The need for higher frequencies and faster switching speed of GaAs FETs has led to a continuous decrease of the gate length down to a few tenths of a micron in some nowadays commercially available discrete devices. But both experimental results and numerical simulations show that for gate length to channel thickness ratios L/a < 3 the influence of two-dimensional effects drastically affects essential device characteristics such as saturation behaviour and threshold voltage. In this paper it is shown by numerical simulations and by experiments that GaAs MESFETs ^ith^channel electron concentrations up to 10 cm can successfully be used to circumvent the difficulties and improve especially the submicron device behaviour. It is demonstrated that even for sub half micron gates the threshold voltage of highly doped FETs remains nearly constant.

articleTitle: Submicrometer GaAs Digital ICs
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Significant improvement in the speed performance of GaAs digital circuits can be achieved with submicrometer design rules. This paper discusses the potential impact of submicrometer design rules on the performance of logic circuits as a function of chip complexity and presents experimental results to verify these conclusions.

articleTitle: GaAs FET Channel Structure Investigation using MBE
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The effects of channel profile and structure on Gm linearity, Gm/Cgs ratio, and the output resistance of GaAs FETs were investigated through the use of molecular beam epitaxy (MBE). An impulse type doping profile was used to fabricate a GaAs FET and found to give very linear Gm resulting in a 15 dB improvement in second-harmonic distortion as compared to our standard ion implanted profile. Channel layers with differing doping concentrations were grown to study doping effects on the Gm/Cgs ratio. GaAs FETs with different gatelength (L) to channel depth (a) ratios (L/a) were fabricated with channel structures which incorporated P-N sub-channel dipole layers or AlGaAs and GaAs buffer layers to investigate mechanisms affecting the drain output resistance Rd. Substantial increases in output resistance are achieved through channel modification.

articleTitle: Monolithic Laser/FET and PIN/FET as Optoelectronic Integrated Circuits (OEIC's) by AlGaAs/GaAs Heterostructures
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Two fundamental units of GaAs-based OEIC's, namely, laser/FET and PIN/FET have been fabricated and tested. The integrated structure of MBE-grown multiquantum-well laser and FET's has realized a low CW current threshold (20 mA) and a high voltage-to-light power transfer ratio (3.3 mW/V). A reasonable current amplification characteristic has been obtained by the PIN/FET structure developed by MOCVD. Both units have successfully operated with the response time less than 1 ns.

articleTitle: A 432-CELL SDFL GaAs Gate Array Implementation of a Four-Bit Slice Event Counter with Programmable Threshold and Time Stamp
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A 432-cell GaAs gate array has been built and personalized to implement a four-bit slice count and compare function. Each cell in the array can be programmed to perform one of three logic operations, and ring oscillator results show a nominal gate delay of 250 ps at 3 mW per cell. The array also contains programmable I/o buffers and 64 bits of SRAM. The cells of the array were designed for efficient routing, and a custom CALMA menu was developed to personalize the array. The array personalization consists of 10 macrocells with each utilizing between 17 and 60 cells for a total of 292 cells or 336 equivalent gates.

articleTitle: GaAlAs/GaAs Integrated Optoelectronic Transmitter using Selective MOCVD Epitaxy and Planar ION Implantation
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The development of a GaAlAs/GaAs integrated laser/MESFET transmitter which operates at frequencies in excess of 1 GHz is described. Such a device is the basis for realizing high-performance integrated optoelectronic transmitters, receivers, and transceivers with on-chip GaAs multiplexers, demultiplexers, and logic functions. A selective GaAlAs/GaAs optical device epitaxy technique, based on metalorganic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD), and planar ion implanted GaAs devices were utilized to monolithically integrate double heterostructure lasers with implanted MESFET drivers. This integration scheme was formulated for potential compatibility with present GaAs IC designs such as buffered FET logic (BFL) and Schottky diode/FET logic (SDFL) circuits which require selective, multiple implants, and small gate geometries. Details of the monolithic integration technique, the characteristics of integrated laser and MESFET components, and the operational characteristics of the integrated transmitter are described.

articleTitle: Exploitation of Gallium Arsenide Digital Integrated Circuits in Wideband Signal Processing Environments
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The emerging application of Gallium Arsenide digital integrated circuits to signal processing problems will require the development of architectures turned to its special characteristics. Chip design methods may be similar to those used for silicon VHSIC components, but system design, packaging and interconnect constraints will be unique to GaAs.

articleTitle: GaAs MSI with JFET DCFL
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A GaAs JFET MSI circuit composed of 500 DCFL gates was successfully fabricated, and it exhibited good performance with high fabrication yield as expected. The MSI chip contains a 4×4 bit parallel multiplier of 156-gates, a 10 bit accumulator of 265-gates and a 8 bit shift register of 90-gates. The chip measures 4.9 mm×3.9 mm in size including bonding pads. Functionality testing of the circuit was done by applying a square wave input and confirmed all gates were working. Highspeed performance of the multiplier and the accumulator was evaluated by the time required for the signal to propagate through the critical path loop. The minimum delay through the critical path in the multiplier was 3.5 nsec with a power dissipation of 70 mW. The accumulator operated in 7.5 nsec with a power dissipation of 57 mW.

articleTitle: A High Performance 1.8 GHz Strobed Comparator for A/D Converter
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A new ultra-high speed GaAs strobed comparator IC has been designed, fabricated and tested. This comparator is designed to be a building block for a 4· bit flash analog to digital converter (ADC) operating at 1.4 GHz clock rate. The operation of such comparator IC's has been successfully demonstrated experimentally up to 1.8 GHz clock rate with a performance suitable for a 4 bit ADC. This clock rate is the highest ever reported for a comparator at room temperature.

articleTitle: Ultra-Low Power, High Speed GaAs 256-BIT Static RAM
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Successful performance of fully decoded low power 256-bit static GaAs RAMs based on depletion-mode MESFET technology.has been demonstrated. Low power RAM cell operation results from the use of a "power concentration" design approach, in which the driver transistor is activated only when the cell is addressed. Considerations for low power cell design include MESFET subthreshold current, which can be calculated using a barrier mode current model, and leakage current in the semi-insulating substrate, which can be prevented by proton bombardment. Operation of 256-bit GaAs RAMs with an access time of 1 ns for 267 mw power consumption is reported.

articleTitle: A High Performance GaAs FET with Shallow N+ Implantation and Recessed Gate for Fast Static Ram
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A nşw GaAs MESFET structure using a shallow n<sup>+</sup> implantation and slightly recessed gate technology was proposed. To decrease the source resistance Rs, the shallow n<sup>+</sup> implantation region was formed between the gate and the source/drain electrodes. The value of Rs was reduced to 4.0 Ω-mm at a 2.0 µm source to gate distance. Also, this structure was applied to 1K bit static RAM, and a 3.8 ns access time with 38 mW power dissipation was obtained.

articleTitle: Buried Channel Acoustic Charge Transport Devices in GaAs
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A new type of charge transfer device is presented, which provides the monolithic realization of signal delay and distributed signal sensing functions in GaAs. Electron transport is accomplished at the sound velocity, in a buried channel defined by a depletion potential, using the traveling wave electric field of a Surface Acoustic Wave (SAW) generated directly in the GaAs. Experimental charge transfer devices based on the Acoustic Charge Transport (ACT) principle have been constructed in GaAs and transfer efficiencies in excess of .996 have been measured at the SAW clock frequency of 360 MHz. In this paper, design considerations for the ACT device are discussed and the charge transfer performance of experimental devices is presented.

articleTitle: An S-Band Phase Shifter using Monolithic GaAs Circuits
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The design and performance of an S-band analogue/ digital phase shifter GaAs IC chip.set, developed for use in a phased array radar transmitter, will be described. The circuits have been used to demonstrate successfully the feasibility of using GaAs IC technology in this application, at a frequency where the more conventional transmission line techniques cannot be used, due to the large size of the circuit elements. The present circuits rely on the use of lumped components, to minimise the area of GaAs used.

articleTitle: A Monolithic 10-GIiz Vector Modulator
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A GaAs transversal filter implementation of a vector modulator is demonstrated at 10 GHz. The magnitude of |S<inf>21</inf>| can be continuously varied from about -40 dB to -10 dB, and the phase angle can be varied to any angle. A method of linearizing the I and Q modulation response is shown to achieve performance appropriate for a 16-QAM modulator. The stage occupies only 0.5 mm<sup>2</sup>, or about 1 mm<sup>2</sup> with area for bond pads and saw kerf.

articleTitle: A 2-8 GHz 2 Watt Monolithic Amplifier
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A 2-8 GHz, 2 watt 10 dB gain power amplifier has recently been designed and tested which utilizes a new and unique GaAs power FET device design, a slow-wave transmission line matching structure and large capacitance (1340 pF/mm<sup>2</sup>) tantalum pentoxide capacitor processing technology. The two-stage power amplifier with input, interstage, and output matching as well as bias circuitry is included on a 7.7 mm<sup>2</sup> <inf>×</inf> 0.1 mm chip. Initial results from amplifier chips designed with approximated FET S-parameters show 10 to 13 dB gain from 1.7 to 8 GHz. Maximum output power of 2 watt was achieved at 2 dB compression with 20% power-added efficiency.

articleTitle: Position and Bias Dependence of Transient Radiation Effects in GaAs Devices
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The response of GaAs field-effect transistors to ionizing radiation transients has been investigated. The position and bias dependences of this response were studied using localized excitation generated by a focussed electron-beam. Two distinct response mechanisms have been identified: one is a positive photoconductive transient due to excitation proximate to the FET channel, and the second is a negative "backgating" transient due to photoconductance through the substrate. The effect of excess deep levels in the substrate and at the active channel-substrate junction is considered.

articleTitle: A Self-Aligned GaAs MESFET with W-Al Gate
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Sputter deposited W-Al alloy film was found to be a low-resistive and thermally stable refractory gate metal for GaAs MESFET. The resistivity of 1000Å thick film is 40pftcm, and it forms good Sohottky contact with n-GaAs even after the annealing at 900°C. Using this gate metal, high-performance self-aligned FET's can be fabricated reproducibly. Maximum transconductance achieved in D-FET was 200mS/mm for V<inf>T</inf>=-0.45V, L<inf>g</inf> =1.2µm and ion implantation energy of 60keV. An E/D gate ring-oscillator showed minimum delay time of 25ps/gate with power dissipation of 2.6mW/gate. This paper shows thermal stability of the new refractory gate metal, W-Al alloy film first. Reproducible FET fabrication process, the results of high-g<inf>m</inf> self-aligned FET<sup>1</sup>s and speed performance are involved in this paper.

articleTitle: A Wideband Two Stage Miniature Amplifier
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A two stage 0.2 to 8 GHz monolithic GaAs FET low noise feedback amplifier has been developed with a minimum of 10 dB gain and about 5 dB noise figure. The amplifier chip includes complete bias and matching circuits as well as input and output (I/O) blocking capacitors and is realized in a small area (1.0 × 1.5 mm<sup>2</sup> ). The input and output VSWR is better than 2:1.

articleTitle: Monolithic Microwave Amplifier using a Two-Dimensional Electron Gas F.E.T. a Comparison with GaAs
publicationTitle: 1983 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: We describe the fabrication of a single-stage monolithic circuit amplifier using a hete-rojunction two-dimensional electron gas FET. The same circuit configuration has also been realised on a classical GaAs FET wafer, permitting a direct comparison of the two materials. Both circuits show reasonable performance in X-Band, the GaAs amplifier giving a maximum gain of 7dB as compared to 5dB from the TEGFET, with good input and output matching. For the TEGFET, contact resistance does not seem to be a major problem, and the technology is compatible with conventional I.C. fabrication methods.
